## **Specimen Details**

To systematically conduct the research instruments, the evaluations should be conducted with maintaining the 3 specimens consistently, mainly the Primary test specimens, Raw material specimens, and Control specimens.   
The tests to be done to answer the statement of the problems concerns the 30 end products produced by the semi-automated paper-charcoal briquette production. These specimens will undergo evaluation on dimensions, structure, and chemical ability. The stated evaluation includes: dimensional variance tracking, mass measurement, standardized drop test, burning time measurement, and burning temperature measurement. These 30 specimens stated above are the Primary test specimens.   
Raw material specimens on the other hand, directly affects the primary test specimens as they are the inputs for the semi-automated paper-charcoal briquette production.. These are strictly limited to: charcoal fines, waste paper, and water.  
	Control specimens should be the baseline for the performance of the end products of the semi-automated paper-charcoal briquette production and should be surpassed by the new technology. These are the common store-bought charcoal and the manually produced paper-charcoal briquette.

## **Multiple Constraints**

The execution of this developmental research and the operation of the semi-automated machine are strictly bounded by the following physical, operational, and material constraints:

1. **Environmental and Power Constraints**

| Constraint Name | Description |
| :---- | ----- |
| Off-Grid Infrastructure Constraint  | To ensure deployment viability in resource-constrained areas, the entire hardware architecture is constrained to operate entirely off-grid, drawing its operational energy exclusively from the integrated solar panel and its associated battery bank.  |
| Weather Dependency Constraint  | The system's power generation is strictly dependent on local solar irradiance. Prolonged overcast weather will degrade the charging efficiency of the 100W panel, potentially depleting the 12V 30Ah battery and halting heavy operations (e.g., thermal curing) until recharged.  |

*Table 7\. Environmental and Power Constraints*

2. **Material and Output Constraints**

| Constraint Name | Description |
| :---- | ----- |
| Material Constraint  | The semi-automated pipeline is restricted to processing exactly three input materials: paper waste, residual charcoal fines, and water. |
| Impurities Constraint  | The system is incapable of extracting any water-insoluble impurities in the paper waste prior to the soaking phase. |
| Shape Constraint  | The physical geometry of the final output is strictly limited to a solid rectangular prism designed specifically for cooking. |
| Size Constraint  | The internal molding and linear actuator assembly is engineered to produce a single, standardized briquette size. |

*Table 8\. Material and Output Constraints*

3. **Process and Mechanical Constraints** 

| Constraint Name | Description |
| :---- | ----- |
| Batch Operation Constraint  | The system is constrained to a discrete batch-processing workflow. A new batch of raw materials cannot be loaded or processed until the current briquette has completed its entire manufacturing cycle and has been physically removed from the mold.  |
| Viscosity and Torque Constraint  | The blending capability is limited by the maximum stall torque of the mixing motor. The system relies on the operator to maintain a reasonable paper-to-water ratio; an excessively dry or dense slurry may stall the motor or trigger current overdraws.  |
| Actuator Stroke Constraint  | The fixed stroke length of the linear actuator limits the maximum volume of wet slurry that can be compressed in a single cycle without risking mechanical binding.  |
| Compaction Limit Constraint  | The densification of the briquettes is strictly hard-capped by the maximum mechanical thrust of the installed linear actuator and the structural integrity of its localized mounting brackets.  |
| Thermal Curing Constraint  | The active drying phase is limited by the maximum thermal output of the 50W halogen lamps; therefore, total moisture reduction time remains partially dependent on external ambient humidity and baseline environmental temperatures.  |

*Table 9\. Process and Mechanical Constraints*

4. **Hardware and Sensor Constraints** 

| Constraint Name | Description |
| :---- | ----- |
| Vibration Interference Constraint | The precision of the HX711 load cell is constrained by physical noise; heavy vibrations generated by the pulverizer and mixing motors may induce minor reading fluctuations during simultaneous motor operation. |
| Volumetric Resolution Constraint | The automated water intake is constrained by the physical resolution of the flow meter, limiting the system from dispensing precise microliter-level measurements. |
| Thermal Sensing Constraint | The DS18B20 temperature probes measure localized ambient temperature within the drying enclosure, rather than the internal core temperature of the molded briquettes themselves. |

*Table 10\. Hardware and Sensor Constraints*

5. **Embedded System and Interface Constraints**

| Constraint Name | Description |
| :---- | ----- |
| Microcontroller Processing Constraint  | The system is constrained to the computational limits of the ESP32-WROOM-32D, utilizing a dual-core architecture to strictly separate asynchronous network tasks from deterministic physical control logic to prevent system latency.  |
| Storage Media Constraint  | Localized data logging is strictly limited to an external FAT32 formatted micro-SD card utilizing an append-only Comma-Separated Values (CSV) structure, as the microcontroller lacks the RAM required to run standard relational database engines (SQL).  |
| HMI Display Constraint  | The physical Human-Machine Interface (HMI) is constrained to a 4.3-inch touchscreen, limiting the on-machine rendering of complex, high-density analytical graphs and requiring the PWA for deeper data extraction.  |

*Table 11\. Embedded System and Interface Constraints*

6. **Software and Network Constraints**

| Constraint Name | Description |
| :---- | ----- |
| Network Connectivity Constraint  | The system operates strictly as a localized Edge IoT node; it does not possess cellular or wide-area network (WAN) connectivity, entirely preventing the transmission of telemetry data to remote internet or cloud servers.  |
| Wireless Client Constraint  | The localized Software Access Point (SoftAP) broadcasted by the microcontroller is constrained to reliably support a maximum of 4 to 5 simultaneous connected mobile devices for monitoring the Progressive Web App (PWA) dashboard.  |
| Web Application Dependency Constraint  | Because the system operates entirely off-grid, the PWA must be fully self-contained within the microcontroller's internal LittleFS partition, explicitly prohibiting the use of external Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) for fonts, icons, or CSS frameworks.  |

*Table 12\. Software and Network Constraints*

7. **Human-Machine Operational Constraints** 

| Constraint Name | Description |
| :---- | ----- |
| Loading Constraint  | The system relies on the operator to manually feed the raw biomass materials (shredded waste paper and charcoal fines) into the designated hoppers, as the machine lacks an automated bulk material intake mechanism. |
| Decision Constraint  | The operator is required to manually authorize the transition between each manufacturing stage. This is executed exclusively through the touchscreen GUI.  |
| Notice & Alert Constraint  | The system is limited to utilizing audio-visual cues only to prompt the user to either proceed to the next automated sequence or revert to a previous state.  |

*Table 13: Human-Machine Operational Constraints*
